e: CloudWatch dashboard sharing lets you give specific people (by email) or a public link read-only access to just that dashboard, with no AWS account or IAM user needed. This is the narrowest permission scope. IAM users with ReadOnly/ViewOnly policies grant broader access, and a bastion host is unnecessary and insecure.

IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) can use AWS Managed Microsoft AD, which connects to the on-premises self-managed AD through a trust, so users and groups stay managed on premises. A one-way trust (AWS Managed AD trusting the on-prem domain) is enough for authentication. Option D adds an IdP that the company doesn't need, and C alone gives no multi-account SSO.

Global Accelerator supports UDP and routes users to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint with fast automatic failover. An NLB handles UDP traffic, while an ALB does not. CloudFront and Route 53 weighted/latency records do not give UDP acceleration or fast failover.

The database is used only 48 hours a month, and stopping an RDS instance stops the instance-hour charges (storage is still billed), keeping the same instance class. Stopped instances restart automatically after 7 days, which fits a monthly cycle. Auto Scaling doesn't apply to a single instance, snapshot/restore is more work, and downsizing reduces compute and memory.

AWS Config managed rules such as required-tags continuously evaluate EC2, RDS, and Redshift resources and flag non-compliant ones with almost no code or infrastructure. The other options require manual work or custom code that must be maintained.

A static website made of HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images can be hosted directly from an S3 bucket at very low cost with no servers. Fargate, EC2, and ALB with Lambda all add compute costs for content that doesn't need server-side processing.

Kinesis Data Streams provides scalable near-real-time ingestion, and multiple consumers can read the same stream. A Lambda function can strip sensitive data before writing to DynamoDB, a low-latency document database. DynamoDB has no write-time redaction rule, Firehose delivers rather than supports multiple custom consumers, and S3 batch processing is not near real time.

AWS Config records and tracks resource configuration changes over time. AWS CloudTrail records the history of API calls made on resources. The other options swap the roles or use CloudWatch, which monitors metrics and logs rather than recording API call history.

AWS Shield Advanced provides detection and mitigation for large-scale DDoS attacks on resources such as ELB, CloudFront, and Elastic IPs, with response team support. The DNS is third-party, so Route 53 protection isn't relevant. GuardDuty and Inspector do not mitigate DDoS attacks, and Shield Standard is basic only.

To encrypt and decrypt data in both Regions with the same key, you need a multi-Region KMS key, which has the same key ID and key material in each Region. B is the only option that uses one. Separate customer managed keys per Region (D) are different keys, and SSE-S3 doesn't use a customer managed key.

Systems Manager Session Manager gives secure shell access through IAM permissions with no open inbound ports, SSH keys, or bastion hosts, and works as a repeatable process aligned with the Well-Architected Framework. Serial console, bastion hosts, and VPN with SSH keys involve more management and a larger attack surface.

CloudFront caches static content at edge locations worldwide, reducing latency cost-effectively, and Route 53 can alias to it. Replicating the bucket to every Region is expensive and complex, Global Accelerator can't use S3 buckets as endpoints, and Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, not website reads.

Heavy write load and slow inserts point to storage IOPS limits on General Purpose SSD. Provisioned IOPS SSD delivers consistent, high IOPS for write-intensive databases. A memory-optimized class or burstable class doesn't fix storage performance, and read replicas help reads, not inserts.

Kinesis Data Firehose is fully managed and highly available, ingesting data and delivering it to S3 without servers. An S3 Lifecycle rule archives data older than 14 days to Glacier, at low cost and with minimal operations. EC2, OpenSearch with manual snapshots, and SQS-based custom consumers all add infrastructure or operational work.

Amazon AppFlow is a managed service that transfers data between SaaS applications and S3, removing the need for EC2 to receive and upload data, and S3 event notifications via SNS handle upload alerts. This offloads the work with the least operational overhead. Scaling EC2 or containerizing keeps the custom code, and EventBridge rules can't pull data from SaaS sources into S3 like this.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 lets instances reach S3 privately and at no charge, bypassing the NAT gateway, which removes NAT data processing and cross-AZ transfer charges for S3 traffic. More NAT gateways or a NAT instance still process the traffic, and a Dedicated Host doesn't affect data transfer costs.

A dedicated Direct Connect link gives a private high-bandwidth path for backups, so internet bandwidth used by internal users is unaffected, and it's a long-term solution. A VPN still uses the internet, daily Snowball devices are impractical, and S3 has no service limit that causes bandwidth problems.

Versioning keeps previous versions so a deleted object can be recovered, and MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete versions or change versioning state. Bucket policies, default encryption, and lifecycle policies don't prevent accidental deletion on their own.

Subscribing an SQS queue to the SNS topic and having Lambda read from the queue makes ingestion durable: messages persist and are retried if processing fails due to transient network issues, so no data is lost. Lambda already runs across AZs, and more CPU, memory, or provisioned concurrency doesn't recover failed deliveries.

Amazon Macie automatically discovers and classifies PII in S3 objects using managed identifiers, with no custom development. Findings can trigger SNS notifications to administrators. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not PII, and custom Lambda scanning of files up to 200 GB is high effort.

An On-Demand Capacity Reservation guarantees EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration, which suits a one-week event. It must specify the AZ. Regional Reserved Instances don't reserve capacity, and a 1-week need doesn't fit a 1-year or 3-year commitment.

Instance store data is lost when the instance stops or fails. Amazon EFS is a durable, highly available shared file system across multiple AZs. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, a bigger instance store is still ephemeral, and Glacier Deep Archive is for archives, not live catalog access.

Intelligent-Tiering suits randomly accessed files in the first year, and a lifecycle rule moves files to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after a year, which is cheap and tolerates retrieval delay. Athena queries recent files in S3, and S3 Glacier Select queried archived ones (note: Glacier Select has since been retired for new customers). Instant Retrieval or Deep Archive with RDS metadata cost more or add complexity.

Run Command executes a command on all 1,000 instances immediately, so a custom patch command can be applied as fast as possible. Patch Manager and maintenance windows are designed for scheduled operating system patching, and Lambda cannot directly run commands on the instances.
